text: On October 26 Anthropic filed its registration statement with the SEC ahead of a Nasdaq listing, and for the first time the price of the most valuable private AI company could be checked against audited accounts. Five months earlier the company had raised $65 billion at a valuation of $965 billion. Its revenue for the whole of 2025 was $4.59 billion. That is 210 times revenue. Measured the other way the same round allows, it is 21. The other way is run-rate, recent sales annualised, which Anthropic put above $47 billion when it announced the Series H . The filing shows the run-rate was no one-month spike. Revenue in the first half of 2026 was $16.29 billion, 14 times the same half a year earlier and more than three times all of 2025. When two honest multiples for one company differ tenfold, last year's accounts are not what anyone is paying for. The US labs are priced on the slope of the revenue line, and on a bet about how long it stays that steep. This part asks what rate the market pays for a slope, and whose money pays it. The nine companies are the American labs whose main business is a model or a product built on one; the AI divisions of Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft do not report revenue separately and are left out. Every figure, with its basis, is in the table at the end. The cleanest measurement comes from Cognition, which makes the coding agent Devin, because it was priced twice in four months. In May it raised at $26 billion on a run-rate it put at $492 million. In September it raised again at $48 billion, with the run-rate at about $900 million. Both numbers had nearly doubled. The ratio between them stayed at 53. The September investors paid the same rate on a bigger number. You do that when you expect the curve to keep its shape. Most of the market sits near that rate. Runway does not publish revenue, but Sacra estimated it at about $96 million annualised at the end of 2025, which puts its February round at about 55 times. OpenAI's March round valued it at 65 times its 2025 revenue, the audited figure that leaked in June . Because that revenue is a full past year rather than a current rate, the multiple on OpenAI's sales today is lower by however much it has grown since. Perplexity, at 100 times reported recurring revenue in September 2025, is the most expensive of the group. xAI also comes out at 65 times, on Sacra's estimate of about $3.8 billion annualised. The price behind that ratio, though, was set in February when SpaceX bought xAI in an all-stock deal, and Elon Musk controls both companies. A price agreed between two companies with the same owner is not a market price.
